description: We are building an interactive Planetary Similarity Index & Earth–Moon 3D Comparison platform for the Artemis mission. Instead of relying on superficial visual comparisons, our tool cross-references real NASA Earthdata (ASTER, SRTM, MODIS) with Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter datasets (LOLA, LROC, M3) to mathematically score and visualize top lunar/planetary analog sites in Chile side-by-side in 3D against real lunar landing zones.
summary:
1. The Problem: Open Access vs. Actual Understanding
Although NASA is at the forefront of Open Science policies, there is currently a critical gap between having access to data and being able to understand or use it.
Fragmentation: Information on terrestrial analogues (sites on Earth with geological or environmental conditions similar to those on the Moon or Mars) is scattered across multiple technical repositories, isolated academic articles and complex databases (such as the Planetary Data System).

2. The Solution: A Unified, Visual and Collaborative Platform
Our tool transforms raw, technical data into an intuitive and actionable experience through three pillars:
Centralisation focused on Artemis IV
‘Progressive Disclosure’ Design (Sliders + View More)
Active Citizen Science: By making the similarity criteria understandable, the platform enables users to propose and validate new analogous sites in their own regions, accelerating global cataloguing.


3. How does our project benefit NASA?

Compliance with the Transform to Open Science (TOPS) initiative 
Optimisation of resources for the Artemis Programme
Inspiring the ‘Artemis Generation’ (Gamification)

‘NASA has already provided us with the open data; our project gives humanity the key to understanding it. By bringing together the lunar South Pole and Mars analogues on a visual, collaborative and gamified platform, we are accelerating research for Artemis IV whilst training the next generation of space explorers.’
details: With our tool the user can compare places on earth with intended landing sites on Luna and Mars. The benefits will be that it will contain in one place data that as of right now is scattered in different papers and isolated sources. The idea is to use it as a tool for science communication so that more people can learn about the artemis mission and explore the viability of different locations as analogs for lunar landing sites. People can add new possible analog sites using real data sources to make sure of the validity of new additions. In addition it has a quiz that tests the users knowledge on already existing analogs on earth. We developed a Mockup using v0.app, however the fully working version of the software is still future work. Our team considered the hard to understand nature of the data that is available from NASA and the difficulty of getting a grip on them. We want to give access to more people to take part in finding new planetary analogs for the future.
